facts.fact: According to the IAB's viewability definition, a display ad is viewable if at least 50% of the ad is in view for 1 second.
facts.quote: At least 50% of the display ad is in view for 1 second.

facts.fact: According to the IAB's viewability definition, a video ad is viewable if at least 50% of the ad is in view for 2 consecutive seconds.
facts.quote: At least 50% of the video ad is in view for 2 consecutive seconds.

facts.fact: Per a third-party eMarketer source cited by StackAdapt, more than 4 in 10 respondents admitted the industry could do better in explaining what viewability is.
facts.quote: with more than 4 in 10 respondents admitting the industry could do better in explaining what it is.

facts.fact: In StackAdapt's illustrative example, one partner identifies 60% of all inventory as viewable impressions, which would leave 40% unmeasurable or unclassified.
facts.quote: For example, one partner might identify 60% of all inventory as viewable impressions.

facts.fact: StackAdapt's blog states that the Media Ratings Council (MRC), together with the IAB, has compiled viewable impression ad measurement guidelines.
facts.quote: In conjunction with the IAB, The Media Ratings Council (MRC) has compiled a list of viewable impression ad measurement guidelines

facts.fact: StackAdapt's article was published on January 31, 2019.
